summary: Taylor County, WI 100-foot steel fire tower erected 1934; staffed seasonally into 2015; listed as standing; sources disagree on which agency runs it.

facts.design: 100-foot steel fire tower with a communications building at its base
facts.agency: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Medford District (Forest Lookouts); Medford branch of the Wisconsin DNR (Star News, 2015)

staffing.status: seasonal: staffed 15 to 20 days each spring

events.note: 100-foot steel tower erected; Forest Lookouts gives 1934 and the WHS record gives Year Built 1934
Perkinstown and Rib River towers staffed 15 to 20 days each spring; one spotter had worked Perkinstown for nine seasons
DNR press release dated December 16, 2015 set out plans to close the state's remaining fire towers
Wisconsin FFLA chapter report: DNR tower divestment is underway; it is yet to be seen whether the agency will retain any towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts lists the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Medford District; the Star News says the Medford branch of the DNR manages the tower. The story reports both and does not pick one.
Forest Lookouts and the WHS record both give 1934. The Star News calls the tower built before 1960, which does not conflict with 1934.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1934 is corroborated by two sources (WHS record and Forest Lookouts). The brief's agency field reflects only the Forest Lookouts page; the 2015 Star News article says the Medford DNR branch manages the tower, so the agency is contested. Access level and current condition are not in any source read, so access is omitted. The 2019 chapter report's 'all are presently planned for removal' sentence follows its account of the seven historic towers it submitted to the WHS, so the story does not treat it as a statement about every DNR tower. The 2019 chapter report does not name individual towers. The Star News piece is a 2015 reprint on usgennet.org; the original is The Star News (Medford, WI), December 31, 2015. No NRHP listing was found.
